Your FICO score (an acronym for the credit scoring service, Fair Isaacs Company) is an assigned number between 300 and 850 that indicates to lenders your capacity to repay a loan. It can change regularly, as new information is sent by your creditors to one or more of the three major national credit bureaus, Experian, Trans Union, and Equifax. The higher your FICO score, the more likely you will qualify for a mortgage loan and the best interest rates.
A FICO score is comprised of 5 parts:

Your types of accounts and your payment record; any bankruptcies, legal judgments, wage garnishments, etc.; the severity and amount of late payments; the number of past-due items and when they occurred. (35%)
How much you currently owe and on what types of accounts; number of accounts with balances; the proportion of credit lines still available. (30%)
Time since accounts opened; by specific type of account; since last activity. (15%)
Number of recently opened accounts, by type and date opened; recent credit inquiries and date of inquiries; reestablishment of good credit after payment delinquencies. (10%)
The number and types of credit accounts available for your use. (10%)
By federal law, you're entitled to a free credit report once every 12 months from each of the three major credit bureaus - Experian, TransUnion, or Equifax.

waitForText.value: Why Use A Small Business Credit Card?

verifyText.value: While consumer and business cards have much in common, business credit cards offer unique benefits to small business owners.
Business cards frequently come with higher credit limits than consumer cards - making them ideal for larger purchases - and may offer flexible payment terms to help businesses maintain cash flow.
Rewards more suitable for business purchases

The majority of business cards come with a points or miles-based rewards program with bonus categories targeted toward common types of business purchases, such as travel, transportation, dining, and office supplies.
Business credit cards report to business credit bureaus, and are an easy way to start building credit for your business.
Business cards also commonly have features that help business owners track and manage their credit card spending, such as spending reports and yearly summaries.
The ability to download transactions to QuickBooks, Quicken and Excel can help automate your bookkeeping.

waitForText.value: Make Smart Use of Your Business Credit Card

verifyText.value: Putting the following good habits into practice can help increase your purchasing power, boost your business credit history, and avoid pitfalls.
By using your card regularly and paying it off in full each month, you can quickly improve your business credit history.

Be proactive and reduce the risk of fraud by regularly reviewing your monthly credit card statements and checking your account online. Notify your card issuer promptly if you spot any erroneous or unrecognized transactions.
Keep spending in check with balance alerts and employee limits

Set up balance alerts for your card and your employees' cards so that you'll be notified by text and/or email whenever your total spending hits a certain threshold that you've set. Only give cards to trustworthy employees who make frequent business purchases, put limits and alerts on these employee cards, and establish clear usage rules.
Putting your personal spending on your business credit card will make it harder to track your business spending and can expose you to personal liability if someone sues your company.
Take advantage of tax deductible interest

Any interest payments you make on the business credit card for business-related purchases are deductible as a business expense. In other words, you can reduce the amount of your business earnings that are subject to tax for these interest payments.

waitForText.value: Which Rewards Program is Best for You?

verifyText.value: Cash back. Free hotel stays. Free or upgraded flights. Figuring out which rewards card will deliver the best payoff for your business spending patterns can seem daunting. Which factors should you consider before applying for a business rewards credit card?

The most popular and straightforward reward is cash back. With a cash back reward program, a percentage of the amount that you spend is paid back to you. Some programs have higher pay back rates in specific categories (e.g. travel, dining, office supplies, etc.) while others offer a flat rate regardless of spending category. Other reward programs give you a certain number of miles or points for purchases that you can redeem for free travel, gift cards, merchandise, or other perks. Savvy small business owners that have the patience, discipline, time or flexibility to hunt out the best redemption opportunities can get incredible deals on these cards.

Other reward programs give you a certain number of miles or points for purchases that you can redeem for free travel, gift cards, merchandise, or other perks. Savvy small business owners that have the patience, discipline, time or flexibility to hunt out the best redemption opportunities can get incredible deals on these cards.

Some cards have huge sign-up bonuses - typically in cash back, points or miles - if you meet the spending requirements within a specific timeframe to qualify for them. These awards can be worth hundreds of dollars in value.

Credit cards come with multiple fees - some are worth paying, others aren't, and most are avoidable. The most common credit card fees include annual fees, balance transfer fees, foreign transaction fees, late payment fees, and cash advance fees. Cards with annual fees tend to have higher rewards structures and higher signup bonuses than those without, so they're worth considering. If you travel overseas at all, you should get a credit card without foreign transaction fees.

Rewards based credit cards are more beneficial to small business owners who pay their credit card statement off every month. These cards generally have higher Annual Percentage Rates (APRs) and if the balance were not paid in full every month, the extra interest would eclipse any rewards earned.
